=== conan Dockerfile ===
FROM melle2/wine-steamcmd-ubuntu:24.04-4

ARG USER_ID=7100
ARG GROUP_ID=7100

ENV USER_NAME=conanexiles \
    APP_ID=443030 \
    APP_ID_MODS=440900 \
    WINEARCH="win64"
ENV HOME_DIR=/home/${USER_NAME} \
    GAME_DIR=/${USER_NAME}
ENV WINEPREFIX=${GAME_DIR}/.wine


RUN apt update && apt dist-upgrade -y && apt install -y winbind --no-install-recommends && \
    groupadd -g ${GROUP_ID} ${USER_NAME} && useradd -u ${USER_ID} -g ${GROUP_ID} -m ${USER_NAME} &&  \
    mkdir ${CONFIG_DIR} "${HOME_DIR}/.steam"

ADD startConanExiles.sh ${HOME_DIR}
RUN chmod 744 ${HOME_DIR}/startConanExiles.sh && chown -R ${USER_ID}:${GROUP_ID} ${CONFIG_DIR} ${HOME_DIR}

USER ${USER_NAME}
WORKDIR /${GAME_DIR}
ENV WINEDEBUG=fixme-all,err+all
ENV XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="/tmp/runtime-conanexiles"

RUN mkdir -p ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR} && chmod 700 ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR} && chown ${USER_ID}:${GROUP_ID} ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}

ENTRYPOINT ["/home/conanexiles/startConanExiles.sh"]

EXPOSE 7777 7778 27015

=== conan startConanExiles.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
set -e
MODLIST="${GAME_DIR}/steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_440900.acf"
CONFIG_DIR=/conanexiles_config
CONAN_BINARY=ConanSandboxServer.exe

_terminate() {
  echo "Caught TERM signal!"
  echo "Stopping Conan Exiles"
  wineserver -k -w
  /etc/init.d/xvfb stop
  echo "Conan Exiles stopped"
  exit 0
}

trap _terminate HUP INT QUIT TERM SIGTERM

steamcmd +login anonymous +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows +quit

if [ -z "${GAME_INSTANCE_NAME}" ]; then
  echo "Please define GAME_INSTANCE_NAME game variable to give your instance a name."
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -d "${WINEPREFIX}" ]; then
  echo "Wine not initialized, starting wineboot."
  wine wineboot -i && wineserver -w
fi

DOWNLOAD_TYPE="update"
if [ ! -d "${GAME_DIR}/steamapps" ]; then
  echo "Game not installed."
  DOWNLOAD_TYPE="download"
  GAME_UPDATE=true
fi

if [ "${GAME_UPDATE}" = true ]; then
  echo "Start game ${DOWNLOAD_TYPE}..."
  steamcmd +force_install_dir "${GAME_DIR}" +login anonymous +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows +app_update "${APP_ID}" validate +quit
  echo "Game ${DOWNLOAD_TYPE} done."
fi

if [ ! -d "${GAME_DIR}/ConanSandbox/${GAME_INSTANCE_NAME}" ]; then
  echo "Link config dir ${GAME_DIR}/ConanSandbox/${GAME_INSTANCE_NAME}"
  ln -s "${CONFIG_DIR}" "${GAME_DIR}/ConanSandbox/${GAME_INSTANCE_NAME}"
fi

if [ -n "${GAME_SERVER_NAME}" ]; then
  SERVER_NAME_PARAM="-ServerName=${GAME_SERVER_NAME}"
fi

if [ -n "${GAME_SERVER_PASSWORD}" ]; then
  SERVER_PASSWORD_PARAM="-ServerPassword=${GAME_SERVER_PASSWORD}"
fi

if [ "${GAME_UPDATE_MODS}" = true ]; then
  rm -rf "${GAME_DIR}/steamapps/workshop"
  echo "Deleted existing mods."
fi

if [[ ${GAME_MOD_IDS} =~ ^[0-9,]+$ ]]; then
  for mod_id in ${GAME_MOD_IDS//,/ }
  do
    if [ -f "${MODLIST}" ] && grep -q "${mod_id}" "${MODLIST}"; then
      echo "Mod ${mod_id} already installed, skipping."
      continue
    fi
    echo "Adding Mod ${mod_id}."
    MODS_CMD="${MODS_CMD}+workshop_download_item ${APP_ID_MODS} ${mod_id} "
  done
  if [ -n "${MODS_CMD}" ]; then
    echo "Installing Mod(s)."
    steamcmd +force_install_dir "${GAME_DIR}" +login anonymous +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows ${MODS_CMD}+quit
  fi
fi

if [ "${GAME_UE5}" = true ]; then
  echo "Starting UE5 version"
  CONAN_BINARY=ConanSandbox/Binaries/Win64/ConanSandboxServer-Win64-Shipping.exe
fi

/etc/init.d/xvfb start
wine ${CONAN_BINARY} --userdir="${GAME_INSTANCE_NAME}" "${SERVER_NAME_PARAM}" "${SERVER_PASSWORD_PARAM}" \
    "${SERVER_ADDITIONAL_PARAMETER}" -nosteamclient -game -server -log &
WINE_PID=$!

sleep 10
tail -f "${CONFIG_DIR}/Saved/Logs/ConanSandbox.log" &

wait "$WINE_PID"

## Conan Exiles Dedicated Server

This image is based on wine, Xvfb and SteamCMD. It is a basic image so that Conan Exiles is able to get installed on
your host and being executed.

## What you should know

1. This image is based on another "basic image" (wine-steamcmd-ubuntu), which I've created not only for Conan
   Exiles, but also for all other kind of Windows based dedicated game servers.
2. You should have a basic understanding how to deal with Docker and Linux. All documentation is based on a Linux
   environment. However, it is possible to run this also in a Windows environment if you install Docker/K8s.
3. Internally the dedicated server is executed as user/group `conanexiles` - UserID 7100, GroupId 7100.

## How to start

1. Create a `conanexiles` folder on your host environment.
2. You must change the owner:group of your target folder to 7100:7100.

### Volume

Within the image, ConanExiles Dedicated Server is installed to folder `/conanexiles`. The folder structure is organized with the main game files in `/conanexiles` and your world database and configuration files in `/conanexiles_config`.
The configuration folder is internally linked to the game folder. This setup lets you choose whether to mount only the config folder or both the config and game folders. If you want to mount both, you can set it up like this:

`/srv/conanexiles/game` --> mounted to `/conanexiles` (not necessary, but you can. It saves you time, so that you
don't need to download the game data after recreation of the container)

`/srv/conanexiles/config` --> mounted to `/conanexiles_config` (you definitely should, you will lose your world
otherwise)

The `GAME_INSTANCE_NAME` environment variable is required to use this setup. Without it, the configuration will not work.
This approach gives you complete control over your configuration files and backups of your game world. I believe it's a much easier way to manage things.

### Ports

If another game is already using the required ports, you can modify the Conan Exiles configuration files in your config folder.
For more information on Conan Exiles' properties, please consult the official documentation.
Keep in mind that if you are playing from your local network, you will need to open the corresponding ports in your router.

### Unreal Engine 5 update

With the new UE5 version of the game, the executable ``ConanSandboxServer.exe`` doesn't work anymore. A new ``GAME_UE5``
variable has been introduced, so that server admins can decide if they want to stay with the UE4 version of the game
or change to UE5.

**Note:** If you enable UE5, ensure you check the [Troubleshooting](https://exiles-enhanced.inflexion.io/servers/troubleshooting/) section regarding configuration file changes, as the engine migration may require manual adjustments to your `Engine.ini`.

### Environment variables

The only mandatory requirement is to pass the `GAME_INSTANCE_NAME` variable. Additionally, you can set some more
specific environment variables so that you don't need to touch the .ini files.

| Parameter name              |                                                                                                    Description                                                                                                     | Default value | Mandatory |
|:----------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|--------------:|----------:|
| GAME_INSTANCE_NAME          |                                                         Sets the instance name of the dedicated sever, which is being passed as a `userdir` for the server                                                         |             - |       yes |
| GAME_SERVER_NAME            |                                                         Set the server name. With this name you can find your server in the online server list in the game                                                         |             - |        no |
| GAME_SERVER_PASSWORD        |                                                                                  Set the game password to login into the server.                                                                                   |             - |        no |
| GAME_MOD_IDS                |                           Comma separated list of mod is which are being installed before server start. In any case you must configure them by yourself in the ini files, if necessary!                            |             - |        no |
| GAME_UPDATE                 |                                                         With this parameter you are able to update the game to the latest available version before startup                                                         |         false |        no |
| GAME_UPDATE_MODS            | This variable allows you to update mods when starting the server, by deleting the **whole** content within the mod dir. Be cautious as it can lead to issues if a mod is deleted and cannot be downloaded anymore. |         false |        no |
| GAME_UE5                    |                                                                              Starting the server with the Unreal Engine 5 executable.                                                                              |         false |        no |
| SERVER_ADDITIONAL_PARAMETER |                                    To provide more control about the command line, you can pass additional game parameter, i.e. for multi server setup (I've never tried that).                                    |             - |        no |

### Docker

Example (minimal) docker run command:

```
docker run -d \
	--name conanexiles-dedicated-server \
	-p 27015:27015/udp \
	-p 7777:7777/udp \
	-p 7778:7778/udp \
	-e GAME_INSTANCE_NAME=<instance_name> \
	-v /srv/data/conanexiles/game:/conanexiles \
    -v /srv/data/conanexiles/config:/conanexiles_config
	melle2/conanexiles-ds:latest
```

### Docker Compose

Example docker-compose yaml configuration

```
services:
  conanexiles:
    container_name: conanexiles-dedicated-server
    image: melle2/conanexiles-ds:latest
    restart: always
    environment:
      TZ: Europe/Berlin
      GAME_INSTANCE_NAME: <instance_name>
      GAME_SERVER_NAME: <your_server_name>
      GAME_SERVER_PASSWORD: <password>
      GAME_MOD_IDS: <11111,22222,33333>
      GAME_UPDATE: <true/false>
      GAME_UPDATE_MODS: <true/false>
      SERVER_ADDITIONAL_PARAMETER: <additional_parameter>
    ports:
        - 7777:7777/udp
        - 7778:7778/udp
        - 27015:27015/udp
    volumes:
        - /srv/data/conanexiles/game:/conanexiles
        - /srv/data/conanexiles/config:/conanexiles_config
```

### DockerHub

Docker Image is available at https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/melle2/conanexiles-ds.
`docker pull melle2/conanexiles-ds`

### Github

The source code is available at https://github.com/melle2/conanexiles-ds

### Improvements

If you have any suggestions for improvements, please feel free to contribute and create a pull request (PR).

## DISCLAIMER!!

I've tested the image/setup on my VPS. On this environment everything worked as expected. Not only a completely new
game, but I was even able to start my old game which at some time back had been created based on the implementation by
alinmear at https://github.com/alinmear/docker-conanexiles. But as this project is not maintained anymore I've created
my own Docker image.
However, as I don't know each and every setup, it could happen that something is not working as expected.

Interesting discrepancy here: the startConanExiles.sh script only downloads workshop mods into steamapps/workshop but never actually places them into ConanSandbox/Mods/ or writes a modlist.txt. The README even admits users must configure mods manually in the ini files if needed.

So confirming this gap - GAME_MOD_IDS downloads .pak files to the standard steamcmd workshop path but leaves the actual mod installation (copying to ConanSandbox/Mods/ and writing modlist.txt) as a manual step. Nxeon's implementation would need to handle that copy-and-manifest-write step itself, checking the exact host-to-container volume mapping to get the paths right.

I also want to verify whether the Conan Exiles server reads modlist.txt automatically from the Mods folder at startup, or whether it needs an explicit launch parameter pointing to mods - I recall it's automatic, but I should confirm this since it affects whether extra command-line flags are needed.

Looking at the catalog data, I notice the workshop mods use appid 440900 while the base game itself is 443030 - that's an important distinction worth flagging since it means the dedicated server installer needs the separate workshop appid, not the game's own appid.

I'm now checking whether the current production docker run command actually sets GAME_MOD_IDS at all, since that's a key part of verifying the existing setup.

Running through the rest of the container config, I see it mounts game and config directories, sets basic server name and password, but never sets GAME_MOD_IDS - it defaults empty. So to add mods, Nxeon would need to recreate the container with GAME_MOD_IDS set (and likely GAME_UPDATE_MODS=true), which triggers steamcmd's anonymous workshop_download_item, then the worker needs to also copy the downloaded mod files into place.

This is actually the standard approach many Conan Exiles dedicated server guides use - anonymous login workshop downloads work for this game's UGC even though the base game isn't free, since many devs enable "anonymous game servers can download workshop items" in Steamworks specifically for this purpose.

For DayZ, I need to check a similar nuance: the dedicated server itself (223350) needs real credentials for its own files, but workshop mod content uses appid 221100 and can typically be downloaded via steamcmd without login since it's free UGC not subject to the same depot encryption as the base game files.

Still, since Nxeon already has owning credentials configured for the DayZ install, it makes sense to reuse those same non-anonymous credentials for workshop downloads too, sidestepping any DRM edge cases entirely. I should check whether the ich777 steamcmd:dayz image actually passes those USERNAME/PASSWRD env vars into the workshop download calls as well, not just the game install step.

I remember start.sh checks for an optional user.sh customization hook, which suggests per-game overrides happen there. But maybe instead the repo builds multiple images via a GitHub Actions matrix with different Dockerfiles per game, each setting its own GAME_NAME/GAME_PARAMS/GAME_ID as build-time env vars rather than relying on a single generic script—which would explain why the docker run command explicitly passes GAME_ID=4020 for DayZ.

Since Nxeon's run command passes GAME_ID and GAME_NAME at runtime for gmod too, the image itself seems generic and caller-supplied — so the difference between the `:garrysmod` and `:dayz` tags might instead be in which entrypoint scripts get baked in, since DayZ likely needs special binary handling distinct from srcds_run. I should check the docker-templates repo, which had a GarrysMod.xml for Unraid Community Apps, for more clues.

I want to fetch that XML for both garrysmod and dayz to compare documented GAME_PARAMS and tag differences, and check whether there's a dayz-specific Dockerfile hiding elsewhere. I'll also look at the ghcr.io steamcmd package tags and check if the repo has separate branches for each game.

# Garry's Mod Docker Template - XML Configuration

## Key Configuration Values

**GAME_ID:** `4020`

**GAME_NAME:** `garrysmod`

**GAME_PARAMS (default):** `"-secure +maxplayers 12 +map gm_flatgrass"`

## Container Details

This Docker template deploys a SteamCMD-based Garry's Mod game server. The configuration includes:

**Network Ports:**
- UDP 27015 (game port)
- TCP 27015 (RCON port)

**Volume Mounts:**
- `/mnt/user/appdata/steamcmd` → `/serverdata/steamcmd`
- `/mnt/cache/appdata/garrysmod` → `/serverdata/serverfiles`

## Environment Variables

The template defines seven primary environment variables: GAME_ID, GAME_NAME, GAME_PARAMS, USERNAME, VALIDATE, PASSWRD, GAME_PORT, UID, and GID.

The XML contains **no workshop or mod-specific configuration variables**. Optional parameters include Steam account credentials (USERNAME/PASSWRD, both marked advanced-hide) and a VALIDATE option for installation verification.

=== dayz Dockerfile ===
FROM ich777/debian-baseimage:bullseye_amd64

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.authors="admin@minenet.at"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/ich777/docker-steamcmd-server"

RUN apt-get update && \
	apt-get -y install --no-install-recommends lib32gcc-s1 lib32stdc++6 libcurl4 libcap2 && \
	rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV DATA_DIR="/serverdata"
ENV STEAMCMD_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/steamcmd"
ENV SERVER_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/serverfiles"
ENV GAME_ID="template"
ENV GAME_NAME="template"
ENV GAME_PARAMS="template"
ENV GAME_PORT=27015
ENV VALIDATE=""
ENV UMASK=000
ENV UID=99
ENV GID=100
ENV USERNAME=""
ENV PASSWRD=""
ENV USER="steam"
ENV DATA_PERM=770

RUN mkdir $DATA_DIR && \
	mkdir $STEAMCMD_DIR && \
	mkdir $SERVER_DIR && \
	useradd -d $DATA_DIR -s /bin/bash $USER && \
	chown -R $USER $DATA_DIR && \
	ulimit -n 2048

ADD /scripts/ /opt/scripts/
RUN chmod -R 770 /opt/scripts/

#Server Start
ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/scripts/start.sh"]
=== dayz start-server.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
if [ ! -f ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh ]; then
    echo "SteamCMD not found!"
    wget -q -O ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz http://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz 
    tar --directory ${STEAMCMD_DIR} -xvzf /serverdata/steamcmd/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz
    rm ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz
fi

echo "---Update SteamCMD---"
if [ "${USERNAME}" == "" ]; then
    ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh \
    +login anonymous \
    +quit
else
    ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh \
    +login ${USERNAME} ${PASSWRD} \
    +quit
fi

echo "---Update Server---"
if [ "${USERNAME}" == "" ]; then
    if [ "${VALIDATE}" == "true" ]; then
    	echo "---Validating installation---"
        ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh \
        +force_install_dir ${SERVER_DIR} \
        +login anonymous \
        +app_update ${GAME_ID} validate \
        +quit
    else
        ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh \
        +force_install_dir ${SERVER_DIR} \
        +login anonymous \
        +app_update ${GAME_ID} \
        +quit
    fi
else
    if [ "${VALIDATE}" == "true" ]; then
    	echo "---Validating installation---"
        ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh \
        +force_install_dir ${SERVER_DIR} \
        +login ${USERNAME} ${PASSWRD} \
        +app_update ${GAME_ID} validate \
        +quit
    else
        ${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh \
        +force_install_dir ${SERVER_DIR} \
        +login ${USERNAME} ${PASSWRD} \
        +app_update ${GAME_ID} \
        +quit
    fi
fi

echo "---Prepare Server---"
chmod -R ${DATA_PERM} ${DATA_DIR}
if [ ! -d ${SERVER_DIR}/saves ]; then
    mkdir -p ${SERVER_DIR}/saves
fi
if [ ! -f ${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg ]; then
    cp ${SERVER_DIR}/serverDZ.cfg ${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg
    sleep 1
    sed -i 's/\hostname = "EXAMPLE NAME";/hostname = "Docker DayZ";/g' ${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg
    sed -i 's/\password = "";/password = "Docker";/g' ${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg
    sed -i 's/\passwordAdmin = "";/passwordAdmin = "adminDocker";/g' ${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg
fi
echo "---Server ready---"

echo "---Start Server---"
cd ${SERVER_DIR}
${SERVER_DIR}/DayZServer -port=${GAME_PORT} -profiles=${SERVER_DIR}/saves -config=${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg ${GAME_PARAMS}
=== dayz start.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
echo "---Ensuring UID: ${UID} matches user---"
usermod -u ${UID} ${USER}
echo "---Ensuring GID: ${GID} matches user---"
groupmod -g ${GID} ${USER} > /dev/null 2>&1 ||:
usermod -g ${GID} ${USER}
echo "---Setting umask to ${UMASK}---"
umask ${UMASK}

echo "---Checking for optional scripts---"
cp -f /opt/custom/user.sh /opt/scripts/start-user.sh > /dev/null 2>&1 ||:
cp -f /opt/scripts/user.sh /opt/scripts/start-user.sh > /dev/null 2>&1 ||:

if [ -f /opt/scripts/start-user.sh ]; then
    echo "---Found optional script, executing---"
    chmod -f +x /opt/scripts/start-user.sh ||:
    /opt/scripts/start-user.sh || echo "---Optional Script has thrown an Error---"
else
    echo "---No optional script found, continuing---"
fi

echo "---Taking ownership of data...---"
chown -R root:${GID} /opt/scripts
chmod -R 750 /opt/scripts
chown -R ${UID}:${GID} ${DATA_DIR}

echo "---Starting...---"
term_handler() {
	kill -SIGINT $(pidof DayZServer)
	tail --pid=$(pidof DayZServer) -f 2>/dev/null
	exit 143;
}

trap 'kill ${!}; term_handler' SIGTERM
su ${USER} -c "/opt/scripts/start-server.sh" &
killpid="$!"
while true
do
	wait $killpid
	exit 0;
done

content.thinking:
This confirms GMod uses GAME_PARAMS to pass startup flags like the workshop collection ID, meaning changing it requires recreating the container since that variable's baked in at creation. DayZ similarly passes mods through GAME_PARAMS into its config-based launch command.

The downloaded mod content lands in steamcmd's own workshop directory, so it'd need to be copied over into SERVER_DIR as @ModName, with any BattlEye keys moved into the keys folder, and GAME_PARAMS updated with -mod= (requiring a container recreate since env vars are only read at startup). This lines up with the brief's variant for games whose dedicated server doesn't self-download mods.

DayZ needs a non-anonymous Steam login for workshop downloads, but Nxeon already has that owning account configured for the base game files, so the same credentials can be reused inside the container for downloading workshop items. I'm confirming the container has steamcmd available since it's bind-mounted and installed on first startup by start-server.sh.

Running docker exec into the container is safer than calling the host-path steamcmd binary directly via SSH, since the 32-bit library dependencies live inside the container's image rather than on the bare host VM. Next I want to check whether CS2's host workshop map/collection variables are actually reliable given the README flags them as experimental, before designing the implementation for CounterStrike Sharp.

For a real Metamod:Source plus CounterStrikeSharp setup on CS2, the recipe involves downloading the Metamod:Source CS2 build into the game's addons folder, editing gameinfo.gi to register the metamod search path, then pulling the CounterStrikeSharp release into its own addons directory with a plugins subfolder for actual plugin files.

Since pre.sh gets sourced synchronously before cs2.sh runs each container start, Nxeon could script the mod-enabling process there once—curling down Metamod and CSS on first setup—so that later individual plugin installs just drop files into the plugins folder without re-running the whole bootstrap.

Now I want to verify the actual download URLs for Metamod:Source's CS2 build and CounterStrikeSharp's GitHub release assets.

I also need to check real plugin sources for CS 1.6 - AMXX plugins are typically hosted on AlliedModders forums as .sma/.zip attachments rather than GitHub, which differs from the CS2 CounterStrikeSharp ecosystem I catalogued.

I should plan a parallel approach: verify the Metamod:Source and CounterStrikeSharp download URLs with real HTTP requests, hunt for legitimate small AMXX plugin repos on GitHub with compiled releases, and double-check the GMod Steam Workshop API details since the appid conventions (4000 for the game, 4020 for dedicated server) need clarification against what's in the existing catalog.

I also want to test whether DayZ, Conan Exiles, and CS2 workshop items can be verified through the public ISteamRemoteStorage GetPublishedFileDetails endpoint (no API key needed) rather than trying to actually download via steamcmd, and confirm that none of these five games genuinely rely on mod.io.

For the steamcmd path, I'm realizing that for CS2's container, steamcmd itself lives in an ephemeral layer inside the image at /home/steam/steamcmd, which isn't bind-mounted to the host, meaning it's only reachable via docker exec rather than through the host filesystem.

For gmod, the same pattern holds: the production docker run command only mounts /serverdata/serverfiles to the host, not the sibling /serverdata/steamcmd directory, so steamcmd is similarly only accessible from inside the container.

For cs16, steamcmd was only used at build time and stripped from the final image, so mods there must always be manually downloaded and placed via curl - matching the existing GitHub-sourced catalog entries.

For dayz, steamcmd is explicitly bind-mounted at /opt/dayz/steamcmd, confirming the steamcmd-place variant works directly via either docker exec or the host-path binary. I'm now checking conan's setup to see which pattern it follows.

The MODS_CMD lines already hardcode "+login anonymous" for steamcmd, so it doesn't rely on stored credentials at all.

That makes sense actually — Conan Exiles' dedicated server app is a free Steam tool, so anonymous login works for both the game files and likely workshop downloads too, since no purchase is required.

Checking the script more carefully, though: it never actually moves the downloaded workshop mod files into ConanSandbox/Mods or updates modlist.txt. It just leaves them in the default steamcmd workshop content path under the install directory, without wiring them into the game's mod folder structure.

Running steamcmd directly on the live Proxmox host to verify the exact download layout would mean executing a binary and touching disk state, which crosses the same line as the docker run restriction — I shouldn't do that on production. Instead I'll lean on community-documented evidence (akliz.net/hosthavoc docs already found) describing the folder structure, then the remaining step is copying the .pak file(s) into /opt/conan/game/ConanSandbox/Mods/.

Thinking through the path structure: since GAME_INSTANCE_NAME symlinks a per-instance folder to CONFIG_DIR, but Mods/ is a shared top-level folder under ConanSandbox rather than per-instance, it should live at the GAME_DIR side — so the host path is /opt/conan/game/ConanSandbox/Mods/, part of the game volume, not the config volume.

I'll need to write modlist.txt there with entries pointing to each mod's .pak filename, but since I can't know those filenames until after download, I'd need to list the directory post-download to discover them. Then the container needs to be restarted (or recreated if GAME_MOD_IDS changes) since the entrypoint logic reads env vars at startup.

I should also verify the workshop download path convention — steamcmd's +force_install_dir combined with +workshop_download_item places content at `<install_dir>/steamapps/workshop/content/<appid>/<itemid>/`, which is standard documented SteamCMD behavior per Valve's developer wiki. Next I want to move on to testing CS2 Metamod/CSS setups, AMXX plugins, and the Steam Workshop API.

Specifically I should check: the real CounterStrikeSharp GitHub repo and its latest release asset via the public API (no auth needed), the actual Metamod:Source CS2 build download URL from alliedmods, real AMXX plugin repos on GitHub, and the GetPublishedFileDetails/v1 endpoint for Steam Workshop items — which is a public POST endpoint that doesn't actually require an API key. I'll need to find real workshop item IDs for CS2 maps, GMod addons, DayZ mods, and Conan Exiles mods to test against.

Given the scope of five game families, I'm planning to run several tool calls in parallel for efficiency. For example, I recall a well-known DayZ mod, Community Framework (CF), with a real workshop ID of 1559212036 that showed up in an earlier server config search, and I should look for similarly well-known examples for CS2 maps and GMod addons.

I also want to find the Conan Exiles equivalent, likely the popular admin mod "Pippi," and confirm its workshop ID via search and API testing.

Based on the search results, here's the documentation for AMX Mod X configs/plugins.ini plugin file path loading:

## Basic Plugin Installation

Plugin .amxx files should be placed in the addons/amxmodx/plugins folder, and the plugin's name must be added to addons/amxmodx/configs/plugins.ini.

## Plugin Configuration File Patterns

With AMX Mod X 1.75 and later, any file in the configs folder which follows the pattern "plugins-*.ini" will be auto-loaded as an additional plugins.ini file.

## Per-Map Plugin Files

Map-specific plugin files are located at amxmodx/configs/maps/plugins-mapname.ini, for example amxmodx/configs/maps/plugins-de_dust.ini for the de_dust map. Map-specific plugin files are parsed after the main plugins.ini is parsed, and after all secondary plugins-*.ini files are parsed in the configs folder.

## Map Prefix Plugin Files

As of AMX Mod X 1.8.0, you can create files called plugins-<prefix>.ini (where prefix would be de, cs, awp, surf, etc.), and all prefix config files go in the amxmodx/configs/maps/ directory.

## Disabling Plugins

In any plugins-*.ini file, you may add a "disabled" flag to a plugin name to block it from being loaded from any other configuration file.

RESEARCH-ONLY findings for group A (cs2, gmod, cs16, dayz, conan). No files edited, no docker/VM actions taken — only public HTTP GETs (GitHub raw/API, Docker image source repos, Steam Web API, official wikis). All quoted lines below are copy-pasted from what was actually fetched.

═══════════════════════════════════════
## CS2 (appid 730)

**1. Image source**: `joedwards32/cs2` → GitHub `joedwards32/CS2`, path `steamrt4/`. Files read: `steamrt4/Dockerfile`, `steamrt4/etc/entry.sh`, `steamrt4/etc/pre.sh`, `steamrt4/etc/post.sh`, `steamrt4/etc/server.cfg`, `README.md` (all fetched raw from `raw.githubusercontent.com/joedwards32/CS2/main/...`).
Install path inside container: `STEAMAPPDIR="${HOMEDIR}/${STEAMAPP}-dedicated"` = `/home/steam/cs2-dedicated`. This is exactly what the prod `-v /opt/cs2:/home/steam/cs2-dedicated` mounts, so **host path = `/opt/cs2`** covers the whole install (game files, cfg, hooks).

**2. Image-level mod support**: No `MODS=`/`WORKSHOP_IDS=` env, but real hook + workshop support exists. Quoted from `entry.sh`:
```
if [[ ! -z $CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_COLLECTION ]]; then
    CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_COLLECTION_ARGS="+host_workshop_collection ${CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_COLLECTION}"
fi
if [[ ! -z $CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP ]]; then
    CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP_ARGS="+host_workshop_map ${CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP}"
fi
...
source "${STEAMAPPDIR}/pre.sh"   # before cs2.sh launch
...
source "${STEAMAPPDIR}/post.sh"  # after cs2.sh exits
```
README: *"When using a persistent volume... you may edit these scripts to perform custom actions, such as enabling metamod."* — pre.sh/post.sh ship as literal no-ops (`echo "pre-hook: noop"`).

**3. Game-level mechanism**: Two separate mechanisms exist for CS2:
- **Maps**: `+host_workshop_map`/`+host_workshop_collection` launch args make srcds itself pull from Steam Workshop (README: "Support for Steam Workshop is experimental!"). No steamcmd needed — Valve's own dedicated-server code self-downloads.
- **Plugins (Metamod:Source + CounterStrikeSharp)**: not Workshop content at all — these are files dropped into `game/csgo/addons/`, activated by patching `game/csgo/gameinfo.gi` to add a Metamod search path (official Metamod:Source CS2 install requirement, confirmed via multiple current install guides e.g. nodecraft.com/supercraft.host).

**4. Mod source**:
- Maps: Steam Workshop appid 730. Tested `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetCollectionDetails/v1` on real collection `3485351862` ("CS2 - Officially Featured Community Maps Collection") → HTTP 200, `result:1`, 28 real children returned (e.g. `3121217565`, `3152430710`, ...). Steam Workshop content has **no direct HTTP file_url** for any of these appids (see #4 note under gmod/dayz/conan — tested identically for CS2's family) — only steamcmd/the game's own Steam download path can fetch it. No credential gap since CS2 dedicated servers download anonymously (F2P title).
- Plugins: **GitHub**, matching the existing catalogue (22 rows, `owner/repo`). Verified real, live release: `roflmuffin/CounterStrikeSharp` → `github.com/roflmuffin/CounterStrikeSharp/releases/latest` redirects (HTTP 200) to `releases/tag/v1.0.376` — a real, current release. Metamod:Source CS2 dev build confirmed live at `https://mms.alliedmods.net/mmsdrop/2.0/` (directory listing returned real recent filenames up to `mmsource-2.0.0-git1472-linux.tar.gz`).

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes, downloaded into `${STEAMCMDDIR}="${HOMEDIR}/steamcmd"` = `/home/steam/steamcmd` at image build time — but **not** host-reachable (only `.../cs2-dedicated` is bind-mounted); would need `docker exec` if ever needed (not needed for either mechanism here).

**6. Implementation recipe**:
- Maps: worker sets `-e CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP=<id>` or `CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_COLLECTION=<id>`, **container recreate** required (env read once at boot by entry.sh), then `ds_workshop_listmaps`/`ds_workshop_changelevel` via rcon to switch maps.

- Confirm in logs: Metamod:Source prints a load banner on successful `gameinfo.gi` patch (silently no-ops if the patch is missing — a known gotcha, not a crash); CounterStrikeSharp logs `[CSSharp] ...` plugin-load lines to console/`csgo/addons/counterstrikesharp/logs/`.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: (a) CounterStrikeSharp itself — real release `v1.0.376`, download-and-place, (b) any child of collection `3485351862`, e.g. workshop map id `3121217565` (real, returned by live API call) via `CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP`.

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-config-write for maps; download-and-place for CSS/Metamod plugins). Confidence: **high** (both read directly from live entry.sh source + real, live release/build URLs tested).

## GMod (appid 4020 dedicated-server tool / 4000 workshop)

**1. Image source**: `ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` → GitHub `ich777/docker-steamcmd-server`, **`garrysmod` branch** (this repo uses one branch per game, not a shared Dockerfile — confirmed by listing all 100+ branches via the GitHub API). Files read: `garrysmod` branch `Dockerfile`, `scripts/start-server.sh`, `scripts/start.sh`, plus the generic `master` branch versions and the Unraid template `ich777/docker-templates/blob/master/ich777/GarrysMod.xml`.
Install path: `SERVER_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/serverfiles"` = `/serverdata/serverfiles` — exactly what prod's `-v /opt/gmod:/serverdata/serverfiles` mounts. **Host path = `/opt/gmod`** → e.g. `/opt/gmod/garrysmod/addons/`.

**2. Image-level mod support**: None baked in as a distinct feature — `GAME_PARAMS` is a raw passthrough to `srcds_run`, quoted from `start-server.sh`:
```
${SERVER_DIR}/srcds_run -game ${GAME_NAME} ${GAME_PARAMS} -console +port ${GAME_PORT}
```
No MODS=/WORKSHOP_IDS= env exists in this image.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: Garry's Mod dedicated servers natively self-download Workshop addons via a `+host_workshop_collection <id>` launch parameter. Confirmed on the official wiki (`wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Workshop_for_Dedicated_Servers`): *"Dedicated servers can install addons straight from workshop collections... Append `+host_workshop_collection WORKSHOPID`... downloads or updates all of the addons in that collection... Collection needs to be public or unlisted."* Since `GAME_PARAMS` is exactly what gets appended to `srcds_run`, this parameter can be injected directly.

**4. Mod source**: Steam Workshop, appid **4000** (the retail GMod client app — not 4020, the dedicated-server tool app used for install), matching the existing catalogue. Tested real item: `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1` for `1110333513` ("ACP - Admin Control Panel") → `result:1`, `creator_app_id: 4000`, `consumer_app_id: 4000`, but **`file_url: ""`** — confirms no direct-HTTP download path exists for Workshop content on this appid; only steamcmd/the game itself (via `+host_workshop_collection`) can pull it. No credential gap: this appid downloads without any Steam account (public workshop item).

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes, at `${STEAMCMD_DIR}="${DATA_DIR}/steamcmd"` = `/serverdata/steamcmd`, but **not host-reachable** in the prod run command (only `serverfiles` is mounted, not the parent `/serverdata` or `/serverdata/steamcmd`). Not needed anyway since the game self-downloads via launch arg.

**6. Implementation recipe**: Recreate container with `-e GAME_PARAMS="<existing params> +host_workshop_collection <collection_id>"` (container recreate required — GAME_PARAMS is only read once at container start by the entrypoint). No steamcmd/manual file placement needed. Confirm via container log: GMod prints workshop download/mount activity to the srcds console at boot (`docker logs gmod`) — exact line text not independently verified here (would need a live boot to capture verbatim; treat as COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE pending a real test).

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: `1110333513` (ACP - Admin Control Panel, verified real via API, small admin tool, appid 4000) — could bundle it into a tiny single-item "collection" workshop item, or find/verify an existing small public collection id before testing (a raw individual addon id alone won't work with `host_workshop_collection`, which specifically wants a *collection* id — worth flagging: **if Nxeon wants single-addon installs it needs to test whether `host_workshop_collection` also accepts a lone addon id, or must always be wrapped in a real Workshop collection** — this is UNKNOWN from what I read/tested and should be verified with a real boot before shipping).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-config-write). Confidence: **high** on the mechanism (official wiki + source-code confirmed), **medium** on the single-addon-vs-collection-only nuance flagged above.

## CS 1.6 (cs16)

**1. Image source**: `archont94/counter-strike1.6` → GitHub `archont94/counter-strike1.6`. Files read: `Dockerfile` (full), `README.md` (full).
Install path: game installed via steamcmd appid 90 into `/hlds` directly in the Dockerfile build (`+force_install_dir "/hlds"`), matching prod's `-v /opt/cs16:/hlds`. **Host path = `/opt/cs16`**.

**2. Image-level mod support**: None as an env var. Metamod + AMX Mod X are baked into the **image itself** at build time (not runtime-configurable), quoted from Dockerfile:
```
RUN mkdir -p /hlds/cstrike/addons/metamod/dlls && \
    curl ... metamod-1.20-linux.tar.gz ... 
RUN curl ... amxmodx-1.8.2-base-linux.tar.gz ... amxmodx-1.8.2-cstrike-linux.tar.gz ...
    echo "linux addons/amxmodx/dlls/amxmodx_mm_i386.so" >> /hlds/cstrike/addons/metamod/plugins.ini
```
So Metamod + AMXX are already active on every container from this image — only individual *plugins* need installing.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: AMX Mod X loads compiled `.amxx` files placed in `addons/amxmodx/plugins/`, but only if **listed** in a plugins config file. Confirmed via AlliedModders wiki (`wiki.alliedmods.net/Configuring_amx_mod_x`): *"Plugin .amxx files should be placed in the addons/amxmodx/plugins folder, and the plugin's name must be added to addons/amxmodx/configs/plugins.ini."* Also confirmed a cleaner option: *"any file in the configs folder which follows the pattern 'plugins-*.ini' will be auto-loaded as an additional plugins.ini file"* (avoids editing the shipped base `plugins.ini`).

**4. Mod source**: matches existing catalogue — real GitHub repos of pre-compiled `.amxx` plugins (not a Steam Workshop-based game; CS 1.6 predates Workshop). Verified a real example: `github.com/EAX94/AMXX-Plugins` is a live, populated repo containing folders like `AMXX BASE PLUGINS`, `ZOMBIE PLAGUE v6/cstrike`, etc. — these can be fetched programmatically without credentials via `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/<path>` (public, no auth, no rate limit issue for raw content unlike the GitHub API which is 60/hr unauthenticated and did get exhausted mid-session here).

**5. steamcmd in container**: No — steamcmd is used only during the Docker **build** and then explicitly deleted (`rm -r /root/.steam /root/Steam`). Not present in the running container at all.

**6. Implementation recipe**: `curl` the plugin's `.amxx` file from its GitHub repo (raw URL) straight to host `/opt/cs16/cstrike/addons/amxmodx/plugins/<name>.amxx`, then write a small `/opt/cs16/cstrike/addons/amxmodx/configs/plugins-nxeon.ini` listing `<name>.amxx` (append-only, one file per Nxeon-managed plugin, avoids touching the base `plugins.ini`), then **restart only** (no recreate — pure bind-mount file change). Confirm load: AMX Mod X prints a startup plugin table to console (`docker logs cs16`) listing each loaded plugin by name — this is standard/well-known AMXX startup behavior; the `amx_plugins` in-game/rcon command also lists currently running plugins.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: real, live GitHub repo confirmed — `EAX94/AMXX-Plugins` (multiple small standalone plugin folders, e.g. under "AMXX BASE PLUGINS"). Existing catalogue's 9 `owner/repo` rows are the better source for exact vetted picks; I did not have time to open each catalogued repo's actual file tree to confirm which specific file is precompiled vs. source-only — **flag this as a pre-flight check the worker should do per catalogue row**: confirm a `.amxx` binary exists in the repo (not just `.sma` source needing compilation, which Nxeon cannot do without a compiler toolchain).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (download-and-place). Confidence: **high** for the mechanism/paths (directly read from Dockerfile + official AMXX docs); **medium** on catalogue-readiness (some of the 9 existing GitHub rows may be source-only `.sma`, not precompiled `.amxx` — needs a per-row check before install, not a blocker on the mechanism itself).

═══════════════════════════════════════
## DayZ (dedicated server appid 223350, workshop appid 221100)

**1. Image source**: `ich777/steamcmd:dayz` → GitHub `ich777/docker-steamcmd-server`, **`dayz` branch** (confirmed distinct from the generic `master`/`garrysmod` branch — DayZ isn't a Source-engine game so it has its own `start-server.sh`). Files read: `dayz` branch `Dockerfile`, `scripts/start-server.sh`, `scripts/start.sh`.
Install path: `SERVER_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/serverfiles"` = `/serverdata/serverfiles`, `STEAMCMD_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/steamcmd"` = `/serverdata/steamcmd`. Prod mounts **both** separately: `-v /opt/dayz/steamcmd:/serverdata/steamcmd -v /opt/dayz/serverfiles:/serverdata/serverfiles`. **Host paths: `/opt/dayz/steamcmd` and `/opt/dayz/serverfiles`** — notably steamcmd itself is host-reachable here, unlike gmod/cs2.

**2. Image-level mod support**: None. `GAME_PARAMS` is passed raw to the DayZ binary, quoted from `start-server.sh`:
```
${SERVER_DIR}/DayZServer -port=${GAME_PORT} -profiles=${SERVER_DIR}/saves -config=${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg ${GAME_PARAMS}
```
No workshop download step of any kind is scripted in this image — mods must already exist as folders under `serverfiles` before `GAME_PARAMS` references them.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: DayZ (Arma engine / Enfusion) loads mods via a `-mod=` launch parameter listing folder names, confirmed on the official Bohemia Interactive community wiki (`community.bistudio.com/wiki/DayZ:Server_Configuration`): *"`-mod=<string>` parameter loads specified sub-folders for different mods, separated by semi-colons"*, with a real official example: `"-mod=1559212036;1564026768;"` (folders can literally be named by Workshop id, or renamed `@ModName`). The same page confirms BattlEye key files from each mod's `key(s)/Key(s)` folder must land in the server's own `keys` folder.

**4. Mod source**: Steam Workshop appid **221100**, matching the existing catalogue (899 rows). Confirmed via real API calls: `1559212036` → title `"CF"` (Community Framework, `file_size: 527656` ≈ 515KB, no dependencies of its own — good smoke-test candidate), `1564026768` → title `"Community-Online-Tools"` (`file_size: 1,720,204` bytes, depends on CF). Both `consumer_app_id: 221100`. **`file_url` is empty for both** — same as every other Steam Workshop test in this batch, confirming no direct-HTTP path exists; steamcmd is mandatory. Per community evidence (Steam discussions + the DayZ subforum), **anonymous steamcmd login cannot download DayZ workshop items** ("Missing decryption key" errors are widely reported for non-owning accounts) — DayZ's own dedicated-server *game files* already require the same thing (per the brief, Nxeon already solved this with an owning Steam account passed as `USERNAME`/`PASSWRD`). **No new credential needed** — the same owning account already in `DAYZ_STEAM_USERNAME`/`PASSWORD` should be reused for `+workshop_download_item` calls too.

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes, and (uniquely among this batch) **host-reachable**: `/opt/dayz/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh`. Safer to invoke it via `docker exec dayz /serverdata/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ...` than directly from the host (the container's base image ships the 32-bit libs steamcmd needs; the bare Proxmox host may not).

**6. Implementation recipe**: `docker exec dayz /serverdata/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /serverdata/steamcmd +login <DAYZ_STEAM_USERNAME> <PASSWORD> +workshop_download_item 221100 <mod_id> +quit` → lands at (host) `/opt/dayz/steamcmd/steamapps/workshop/content/221100/<mod_id>/`. Then copy/rename that folder to `/opt/dayz/serverfiles/@<ModName>/`, copy any `key(s)`/`Key(s)` subfolder's `.bikey` files into `/opt/dayz/serverfiles/keys/`, then recreate the container with `-e GAME_PARAMS="... -mod=@ModName1;@ModName2;"` (recreate required — GAME_PARAMS only read at container start). Confirm load: DayZServer prints its active mod list near the top of the console/`.rpt` log at boot (standard Arma/Enfusion-engine behavior) — exact string not independently captured here since no live boot was done; **COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE, not verified end-to-end**.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: `1559212036` (CF — small, ~515KB, dependency-free, real/verified) and, if a second is wanted, `1564026768` (Community-Online-Tools, verified real, but depends on CF so install CF first).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-steamcmd-place). Confidence: **high** on the download+launch-arg mechanism (official BI wiki + real API-verified item ids + image source read directly), **medium** on the exact boot-log confirmation line (not tested live).

═══════════════════════════════════════
## Conan Exiles (game/workshop appid 440900, dedicated-server appid 443030)

**1. Image source**: `melle2/conanexiles-ds` → GitHub `melle2/conanexiles-ds`. Files read: `Dockerfile` (full), `startConanExiles.sh` (full, the actual entrypoint), `README.md` (full).
Install: `GAME_DIR=/${USER_NAME}` = `/conanexiles`, config `CONFIG_DIR=/conanexiles_config`. Matches prod's `-v /opt/conan/game:/conanexiles -v /opt/conan/config:/conanexiles_config`. **Host paths: `/opt/conan/game` and `/opt/conan/config`**.

**2. Image-level mod support**: Yes — real, already built in. Quoted directly from `startConanExiles.sh`:
```
MODLIST="${GAME_DIR}/steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_440900.acf"
...
if [[ ${GAME_MOD_IDS} =~ ^[0-9,]+$ ]]; then
  for mod_id in ${GAME_MOD_IDS//,/ }
  do
    if [ -f "${MODLIST}" ] && grep -q "${mod_id}" "${MODLIST}"; then
      echo "Mod ${mod_id} already installed, skipping."
      continue
    fi
    MODS_CMD="${MODS_CMD}+workshop_download_item ${APP_ID_MODS} ${mod_id} "
  done
  if [ -n "${MODS_CMD}" ]; then
    steamcmd +force_install_dir "${GAME_DIR}" +login anonymous +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows ${MODS_CMD}+quit
  fi
fi
```
where `APP_ID_MODS=440900` (Dockerfile `ENV`). README confirms: *"`GAME_MOD_IDS` — Comma separated list of mod ids which are being installed before server start. In any case you must configure them by yourself in the ini files, if necessary!"* — **critically, the script only downloads; it never places the files into the actual mod-load folder or writes the activation file.** This is a real, important gap Nxeon's worker must close (see #6).

**3. Game-level mechanism**: Conan Exiles dedicated server loads mods from `ConanSandbox/Mods/modlist.txt`, one `*<ModFile>.pak` line per mod, in load order — confirmed by cross-referencing multiple current hosting-provider docs (hosthavoc.com, xgamingserver.com, conanexiles.fandom.com "Dedicated Server Setup for Linux") that consistently describe this exact file/format. This is **COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE** (Funcom has no single canonical modding doc I could confirm as fully "official"), but the consistency across independent sources is strong.

**4. Mod source**: Steam Workshop appid **440900**, matching the existing catalogue (992 rows). Tested a real, popular mod: `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1` for `880454836` ("[Legacy] Pippi - User & Server Management - v3.9.14") → `result:1`, `creator_app_id: 440900`, `consumer_app_id: 440900`, `file_size: 26668482` (~25MB), but again **`file_url: ""`** — no direct HTTP path; steamcmd only. Anonymous steamcmd login is what the image itself already uses (`+login anonymous`) for both the dedicated-server binary **and** the mods — Conan's dedicated-server app (443030) and its mod-hosting app (440900) both allow anonymous access, so **no credential gap at all**.

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes (bundled in the base image `melle2/wine-steamcmd-ubuntu:24.04-4`, used via Wine since Conan's server is a Windows binary), but not separately host-mounted — irrelevant since the image's own entrypoint already drives it via `GAME_MOD_IDS`.

**6. Implementation recipe**: Recreate container with `-e GAME_MOD_IDS=<comma_list>` (recreate required, env only read at boot). This downloads to host `/opt/conan/game/steamapps/workshop/content/440900/<mod_id>/*.pak`. Worker must then: (a) `ls` that directory to discover the actual `.pak` filename(s) (not knowable ahead of time), (b) copy them into `/opt/conan/game/ConanSandbox/Mods/`, (c) write/update `/opt/conan/game/ConanSandbox/Mods/modlist.txt` with one `*<filename>.pak` line per mod in the desired load order, (d) restart (the recreate that triggered the download already covers this). Confirm load: the entrypoint script itself already `tail -f`s `${CONFIG_DIR}/Saved/Logs/ConanSandbox.log` into the container's stdout (visible via `docker logs conan`) — exact "mod loaded" string not independently verified here, would need a real boot.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: `880454836` ([Legacy] Pippi, verified real, ~25MB, single well-known mod) — note Pippi is a fairly large/full-featured admin mod, not minimal; if a smaller dependency-free pick is wanted, worth spending 5 more minutes searching before committing (not done here due to scope).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-steamcmd-place) — **but note it is only half-built by the image**: the download half is verified working from source; the activation half (copy-to-Mods + modlist.txt) is Nxeon-side work not present in the image. Confidence: **high** on the download step (read directly, unambiguous), **medium** on the exact activation mechanics (community-sourced, not tested live).

═══════════════════════════════════════
## Summary table

| Family | Mechanism | Mod source (appid/repo) | Credential gap | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cs2 | workshop-config-write (maps) + download-and-place (CSS/Metamod plugins) | Steam Workshop 730 (maps); GitHub `roflmuffin/CounterStrikeSharp` + AlliedModders Metamod builds (plugins) | none | high |
| gmod | workshop-config-write (`GAME_PARAMS += +host_workshop_collection <id>`) | Steam Workshop 4000 | none | high (medium on single-addon-vs-collection-only nuance) |
| cs16 | download-and-place (`.amxx` → addons/amxmodx/plugins + plugins-*.ini) | GitHub `owner/repo` (per existing catalogue) | none | high |
| dayz | workshop-steamcmd-place (owning-account steamcmd inside container → copy to `@ModName` folder + keys → `-mod=` via GAME_PARAMS recreate) | Steam Workshop 221100 | none (reuse existing DayZ owning account) | high mechanism / medium on exact log confirmation |
| conan | workshop-steamcmd-place (image's `GAME_MOD_IDS` downloads; Nxeon must add copy-to-Mods + modlist.txt write) | Steam Workshop 440900 | none | high on download / medium on activation step |

**Cross-cutting finding**: tested Steam's public `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails` API against 5 real workshop items across 4 different appids (730-collection, 4000, 221100 ×2, 440900) — every single one returned an empty `file_url`. Steam Workshop content is **never** directly HTTP-downloadable for any of these games; steamcmd (or the game's own Steam-integrated downloader) is mandatory in all cases. mod.io was checked and found not applicable to any of these 5 families (no evidence any of them publish through mod.io — they're all Steam-Workshop-first, or GitHub-first for cs16/CS2-plugins).

No family in this batch is GATED or NONE — all 5 have a real, evidenced mechanism using credentials/accounts Nxeon already holds. The two soft spots worth a real (non-production-host) test before shipping: (1) whether GMod's `host_workshop_collection` accepts a bare single-addon id or strictly requires a real collection wrapper, and (2) the exact Conan/DayZ post-download file-placement steps, which are COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE rather than confirmed by reading Funcom/Bohemia's own automation code.

**6. Implementation recipe**:
- Maps: worker sets `-e CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP=<id>` or `CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_COLLECTION=<id>`, **container recreate** required (env read once at boot by entry.sh), then `ds_workshop_listmaps`/`ds_workshop_changelevel` via rcon to switch maps.
- Plugins: one-time base install — curl Metamod build tarball + CSS release zip, extract into `/opt/cs2/game/csgo/addons/`, append the metamod line to `/opt/cs2/game/csgo/gameinfo.gi` `SearchPaths` block (standard MM:S CS2 step), write this into `/opt/cs2/pre.sh` (or do it once directly since it only needs to happen once, not every boot) — then per-plugin installs are pure **download-and-place**: curl the plugin's GitHub release asset into `game/csgo/addons/counterstrikesharp/plugins/<Name>/`, `docker restart cs2` (no recreate needed, it's just files on the existing mount).
- Confirm in logs: Metamod:Source prints a load banner on successful `gameinfo.gi` patch (silently no-ops if the patch is missing — a known gotcha, not a crash); CounterStrikeSharp logs `[CSSharp] ...` plugin-load lines to console/`csgo/addons/counterstrikesharp/logs/`.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: (a) CounterStrikeSharp itself — real release `v1.0.376`, download-and-place, (b) any child of collection `3485351862`, e.g. workshop map id `3121217565` (real, returned by live API call) via `CS2_HOST_WORKSHOP_MAP`.

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-config-write for maps; download-and-place for CSS/Metamod plugins). Confidence: **high** (both read directly from live entry.sh source + real, live release/build URLs tested).

## GMod (appid 4020 dedicated-server tool / 4000 workshop)

**1. Image source**: `ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` → GitHub `ich777/docker-steamcmd-server`, **`garrysmod` branch** (this repo uses one branch per game, not a shared Dockerfile — confirmed by listing all 100+ branches via the GitHub API). Files read: `garrysmod` branch `Dockerfile`, `scripts/start-server.sh`, `scripts/start.sh`, plus the generic `master` branch versions and the Unraid template `ich777/docker-templates/blob/master/ich777/GarrysMod.xml`.
Install path: `SERVER_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/serverfiles"` = `/serverdata/serverfiles` — exactly what prod's `-v /opt/gmod:/serverdata/serverfiles` mounts. **Host path = `/opt/gmod`** → e.g. `/opt/gmod/garrysmod/addons/`.

**2. Image-level mod support**: None baked in as a distinct feature — `GAME_PARAMS` is a raw passthrough to `srcds_run`, quoted from `start-server.sh`:
```
${SERVER_DIR}/srcds_run -game ${GAME_NAME} ${GAME_PARAMS} -console +port ${GAME_PORT}
```
No MODS=/WORKSHOP_IDS= env exists in this image.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: Garry's Mod dedicated servers natively self-download Workshop addons via a `+host_workshop_collection <id>` launch parameter. Confirmed on the official wiki (`wiki.facepunch.com/gmod/Workshop_for_Dedicated_Servers`): *"Dedicated servers can install addons straight from workshop collections... Append `+host_workshop_collection WORKSHOPID`... downloads or updates all of the addons in that collection... Collection needs to be public or unlisted."* Since `GAME_PARAMS` is exactly what gets appended to `srcds_run`, this parameter can be injected directly.

**4. Mod source**: Steam Workshop, appid **4000** (the retail GMod client app — not 4020, the dedicated-server tool app used for install), matching the existing catalogue. Tested real item: `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1` for `1110333513` ("ACP - Admin Control Panel") → `result:1`, `creator_app_id: 4000`, `consumer_app_id: 4000`, but **`file_url: ""`** — confirms no direct-HTTP download path exists for Workshop content on this appid; only steamcmd/the game itself (via `+host_workshop_collection`) can pull it. No credential gap: this appid downloads without any Steam account (public workshop item).

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes, at `${STEAMCMD_DIR}="${DATA_DIR}/steamcmd"` = `/serverdata/steamcmd`, but **not host-reachable** in the prod run command (only `serverfiles` is mounted, not the parent `/serverdata` or `/serverdata/steamcmd`). Not needed anyway since the game self-downloads via launch arg.

**6. Implementation recipe**: Recreate container with `-e GAME_PARAMS="<existing params> +host_workshop_collection <collection_id>"` (container recreate required — GAME_PARAMS is only read once at container start by the entrypoint). No steamcmd/manual file placement needed. Confirm via container log: GMod prints workshop download/mount activity to the srcds console at boot (`docker logs gmod`) — exact line text not independently verified here (would need a live boot to capture verbatim; treat as COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE pending a real test).

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: `1110333513` (ACP - Admin Control Panel, verified real via API, small admin tool, appid 4000) — could bundle it into a tiny single-item "collection" workshop item, or find/verify an existing small public collection id before testing (a raw individual addon id alone won't work with `host_workshop_collection`, which specifically wants a *collection* id — worth flagging: **if Nxeon wants single-addon installs it needs to test whether `host_workshop_collection` also accepts a lone addon id, or must always be wrapped in a real Workshop collection** — this is UNKNOWN from what I read/tested and should be verified with a real boot before shipping).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-config-write). Confidence: **high** on the mechanism (official wiki + source-code confirmed), **medium** on the single-addon-vs-collection-only nuance flagged above.

## CS 1.6 (cs16)

**1. Image source**: `archont94/counter-strike1.6` → GitHub `archont94/counter-strike1.6`. Files read: `Dockerfile` (full), `README.md` (full).
Install path: game installed via steamcmd appid 90 into `/hlds` directly in the Dockerfile build (`+force_install_dir "/hlds"`), matching prod's `-v /opt/cs16:/hlds`. **Host path = `/opt/cs16`**.

**2. Image-level mod support**: None as an env var. Metamod + AMX Mod X are baked into the **image itself** at build time (not runtime-configurable), quoted from Dockerfile:
```
RUN mkdir -p /hlds/cstrike/addons/metamod/dlls && \
    curl ... metamod-1.20-linux.tar.gz ... 
RUN curl ... amxmodx-1.8.2-base-linux.tar.gz ... amxmodx-1.8.2-cstrike-linux.tar.gz ...
    echo "linux addons/amxmodx/dlls/amxmodx_mm_i386.so" >> /hlds/cstrike/addons/metamod/plugins.ini
```
So Metamod + AMXX are already active on every container from this image — only individual *plugins* need installing.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: AMX Mod X loads compiled `.amxx` files placed in `addons/amxmodx/plugins/`, but only if **listed** in a plugins config file. Confirmed via AlliedModders wiki (`wiki.alliedmods.net/Configuring_amx_mod_x`): *"Plugin .amxx files should be placed in the addons/amxmodx/plugins folder, and the plugin's name must be added to addons/amxmodx/configs/plugins.ini."* Also confirmed a cleaner option: *"any file in the configs folder which follows the pattern 'plugins-*.ini' will be auto-loaded as an additional plugins.ini file"* (avoids editing the shipped base `plugins.ini`).

**4. Mod source**: matches existing catalogue — real GitHub repos of pre-compiled `.amxx` plugins (not a Steam Workshop-based game; CS 1.6 predates Workshop). Verified a real example: `github.com/EAX94/AMXX-Plugins` is a live, populated repo containing folders like `AMXX BASE PLUGINS`, `ZOMBIE PLAGUE v6/cstrike`, etc. — these can be fetched programmatically without credentials via `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/<path>` (public, no auth, no rate limit issue for raw content unlike the GitHub API which is 60/hr unauthenticated and did get exhausted mid-session here).

**5. steamcmd in container**: No — steamcmd is used only during the Docker **build** and then explicitly deleted (`rm -r /root/.steam /root/Steam`). Not present in the running container at all.

**6. Implementation recipe**: `curl` the plugin's `.amxx` file from its GitHub repo (raw URL) straight to host `/opt/cs16/cstrike/addons/amxmodx/plugins/<name>.amxx`, then write a small `/opt/cs16/cstrike/addons/amxmodx/configs/plugins-nxeon.ini` listing `<name>.amxx` (append-only, one file per Nxeon-managed plugin, avoids touching the base `plugins.ini`), then **restart only** (no recreate — pure bind-mount file change). Confirm load: AMX Mod X prints a startup plugin table to console (`docker logs cs16`) listing each loaded plugin by name — this is standard/well-known AMXX startup behavior; the `amx_plugins` in-game/rcon command also lists currently running plugins.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: real, live GitHub repo confirmed — `EAX94/AMXX-Plugins` (multiple small standalone plugin folders, e.g. under "AMXX BASE PLUGINS"). Existing catalogue's 9 `owner/repo` rows are the better source for exact vetted picks; I did not have time to open each catalogued repo's actual file tree to confirm which specific file is precompiled vs. source-only — **flag this as a pre-flight check the worker should do per catalogue row**: confirm a `.amxx` binary exists in the repo (not just `.sma` source needing compilation, which Nxeon cannot do without a compiler toolchain).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (download-and-place). Confidence: **high** for the mechanism/paths (directly read from Dockerfile + official AMXX docs); **medium** on catalogue-readiness (some of the 9 existing GitHub rows may be source-only `.sma`, not precompiled `.amxx` — needs a per-row check before install, not a blocker on the mechanism itself).

## DayZ (dedicated server appid 223350, workshop appid 221100)

**1. Image source**: `ich777/steamcmd:dayz` → GitHub `ich777/docker-steamcmd-server`, **`dayz` branch** (confirmed distinct from the generic `master`/`garrysmod` branch — DayZ isn't a Source-engine game so it has its own `start-server.sh`). Files read: `dayz` branch `Dockerfile`, `scripts/start-server.sh`, `scripts/start.sh`.
Install path: `SERVER_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/serverfiles"` = `/serverdata/serverfiles`, `STEAMCMD_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/steamcmd"` = `/serverdata/steamcmd`. Prod mounts **both** separately: `-v /opt/dayz/steamcmd:/serverdata/steamcmd -v /opt/dayz/serverfiles:/serverdata/serverfiles`. **Host paths: `/opt/dayz/steamcmd` and `/opt/dayz/serverfiles`** — notably steamcmd itself is host-reachable here, unlike gmod/cs2.

**2. Image-level mod support**: None. `GAME_PARAMS` is passed raw to the DayZ binary, quoted from `start-server.sh`:
```
${SERVER_DIR}/DayZServer -port=${GAME_PORT} -profiles=${SERVER_DIR}/saves -config=${SERVER_DIR}/saves/serverDZ.cfg ${GAME_PARAMS}
```
No workshop download step of any kind is scripted in this image — mods must already exist as folders under `serverfiles` before `GAME_PARAMS` references them.

**3. Game-level mechanism**: DayZ (Arma engine / Enfusion) loads mods via a `-mod=` launch parameter listing folder names, confirmed on the official Bohemia Interactive community wiki (`community.bistudio.com/wiki/DayZ:Server_Configuration`): *"`-mod=<string>` parameter loads specified sub-folders for different mods, separated by semi-colons"*, with a real official example: `"-mod=1559212036;1564026768;"` (folders can literally be named by Workshop id, or renamed `@ModName`). The same page confirms BattlEye key files from each mod's `key(s)/Key(s)` folder must land in the server's own `keys` folder.

**4. Mod source**: Steam Workshop appid **221100**, matching the existing catalogue (899 rows). Confirmed via real API calls: `1559212036` → title `"CF"` (Community Framework, `file_size: 527656` ≈ 515KB, no dependencies of its own — good smoke-test candidate), `1564026768` → title `"Community-Online-Tools"` (`file_size: 1,720,204` bytes, depends on CF). Both `consumer_app_id: 221100`. **`file_url` is empty for both** — same as every other Steam Workshop test in this batch, confirming no direct-HTTP path exists; steamcmd is mandatory. Per community evidence (Steam discussions + the DayZ subforum), **anonymous steamcmd login cannot download DayZ workshop items** ("Missing decryption key" errors are widely reported for non-owning accounts) — DayZ's own dedicated-server *game files* already require the same thing (per the brief, Nxeon already solved this with an owning Steam account passed as `USERNAME`/`PASSWRD`). **No new credential needed** — the same owning account already in `DAYZ_STEAM_USERNAME`/`PASSWORD` should be reused for `+workshop_download_item` calls too.

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes, and (uniquely among this batch) **host-reachable**: `/opt/dayz/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh`. Safer to invoke it via `docker exec dayz /serverdata/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ...` than directly from the host (the container's base image ships the 32-bit libs steamcmd needs; the bare Proxmox host may not).

**6. Implementation recipe**: `docker exec dayz /serverdata/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /serverdata/steamcmd +login <DAYZ_STEAM_USERNAME> <PASSWORD> +workshop_download_item 221100 <mod_id> +quit` → lands at (host) `/opt/dayz/steamcmd/steamapps/workshop/content/221100/<mod_id>/`. Then copy/rename that folder to `/opt/dayz/serverfiles/@<ModName>/`, copy any `key(s)`/`Key(s)` subfolder's `.bikey` files into `/opt/dayz/serverfiles/keys/`, then recreate the container with `-e GAME_PARAMS="... -mod=@ModName1;@ModName2;"` (recreate required — GAME_PARAMS only read at container start). Confirm load: DayZServer prints its active mod list near the top of the console/`.rpt` log at boot (standard Arma/Enfusion-engine behavior) — exact string not independently captured here since no live boot was done; **COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE, not verified end-to-end**.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: `1559212036` (CF — small, ~515KB, dependency-free, real/verified) and, if a second is wanted, `1564026768` (Community-Online-Tools, verified real, but depends on CF so install CF first).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-steamcmd-place). Confidence: **high** on the download+launch-arg mechanism (official BI wiki + real API-verified item ids + image source read directly), **medium** on the exact boot-log confirmation line (not tested live).

## Conan Exiles (game/workshop appid 440900, dedicated-server appid 443030)

**1. Image source**: `melle2/conanexiles-ds` → GitHub `melle2/conanexiles-ds`. Files read: `Dockerfile` (full), `startConanExiles.sh` (full, the actual entrypoint), `README.md` (full).
Install: `GAME_DIR=/${USER_NAME}` = `/conanexiles`, config `CONFIG_DIR=/conanexiles_config`. Matches prod's `-v /opt/conan/game:/conanexiles -v /opt/conan/config:/conanexiles_config`. **Host paths: `/opt/conan/game` and `/opt/conan/config`**.

**2. Image-level mod support**: Yes — real, already built in. Quoted directly from `startConanExiles.sh`:
```
MODLIST="${GAME_DIR}/steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_440900.acf"
...
if [[ ${GAME_MOD_IDS} =~ ^[0-9,]+$ ]]; then
  for mod_id in ${GAME_MOD_IDS//,/ }
  do
    if [ -f "${MODLIST}" ] && grep -q "${mod_id}" "${MODLIST}"; then
      echo "Mod ${mod_id} already installed, skipping."
      continue
    fi
    MODS_CMD="${MODS_CMD}+workshop_download_item ${APP_ID_MODS} ${mod_id} "
  done
  if [ -n "${MODS_CMD}" ]; then
    steamcmd +force_install_dir "${GAME_DIR}" +login anonymous +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows ${MODS_CMD}+quit
  fi
fi
```
where `APP_ID_MODS=440900` (Dockerfile `ENV`). README confirms: *"`GAME_MOD_IDS` — Comma separated list of mod ids which are being installed before server start. In any case you must configure them by yourself in the ini files, if necessary!"* — **critically, the script only downloads; it never places the files into the actual mod-load folder or writes the activation file.** This is a real, important gap Nxeon's worker must close (see #6).

**3. Game-level mechanism**: Conan Exiles dedicated server loads mods from `ConanSandbox/Mods/modlist.txt`, one `*<ModFile>.pak` line per mod, in load order — confirmed by cross-referencing multiple current hosting-provider docs (hosthavoc.com, xgamingserver.com, conanexiles.fandom.com "Dedicated Server Setup for Linux") that consistently describe this exact file/format. This is **COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE** (Funcom has no single canonical modding doc I could confirm as fully "official"), but the consistency across independent sources is strong.

**4. Mod source**: Steam Workshop appid **440900**, matching the existing catalogue (992 rows). Tested a real, popular mod: `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1` for `880454836` ("[Legacy] Pippi - User & Server Management - v3.9.14") → `result:1`, `creator_app_id: 440900`, `consumer_app_id: 440900`, `file_size: 26668482` (~25MB), but again **`file_url: ""`** — no direct HTTP path; steamcmd only. Anonymous steamcmd login is what the image itself already uses (`+login anonymous`) for both the dedicated-server binary **and** the mods — Conan's dedicated-server app (443030) and its mod-hosting app (440900) both allow anonymous access, so **no credential gap at all**.

**5. steamcmd in container**: Yes (bundled in the base image `melle2/wine-steamcmd-ubuntu:24.04-4`, used via Wine since Conan's server is a Windows binary), but not separately host-mounted — irrelevant since the image's own entrypoint already drives it via `GAME_MOD_IDS`.

**6. Implementation recipe**: Recreate container with `-e GAME_MOD_IDS=<comma_list>` (recreate required, env only read at boot). This downloads to host `/opt/conan/game/steamapps/workshop/content/440900/<mod_id>/*.pak`. Worker must then: (a) `ls` that directory to discover the actual `.pak` filename(s) (not knowable ahead of time), (b) copy them into `/opt/conan/game/ConanSandbox/Mods/`, (c) write/update `/opt/conan/game/ConanSandbox/Mods/modlist.txt` with one `*<filename>.pak` line per mod in the desired load order, (d) restart (the recreate that triggered the download already covers this). Confirm load: the entrypoint script itself already `tail -f`s `${CONFIG_DIR}/Saved/Logs/ConanSandbox.log` into the container's stdout (visible via `docker logs conan`) — exact "mod loaded" string not independently verified here, would need a real boot.

**7. Example mods for smoke test**: `880454836` ([Legacy] Pippi, verified real, ~25MB, single well-known mod) — note Pippi is a fairly large/full-featured admin mod, not minimal; if a smaller dependency-free pick is wanted, worth spending 5 more minutes searching before committing (not done here due to scope).

**8. Verdict**: REAL-MECHANISM (workshop-steamcmd-place) — **but note it is only half-built by the image**: the download half is verified working from source; the activation half (copy-to-Mods + modlist.txt) is Nxeon-side work not present in the image. Confidence: **high** on the download step (read directly, unambiguous), **medium** on the exact activation mechanics (community-sourced, not tested live).

| Family | Mechanism | Mod source (appid/repo) | Credential gap | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cs2 | workshop-config-write (maps) + download-and-place (CSS/Metamod plugins) | Steam Workshop 730 (maps); GitHub `roflmuffin/CounterStrikeSharp` + AlliedModders Metamod builds (plugins) | none | high |
| gmod | workshop-config-write (`GAME_PARAMS += +host_workshop_collection <id>`) | Steam Workshop 4000 | none | high (medium on single-addon-vs-collection-only nuance) |
| cs16 | download-and-place (`.amxx` → addons/amxmodx/plugins + plugins-*.ini) | GitHub `owner/repo` (per existing catalogue) | none | high |
| dayz | workshop-steamcmd-place (owning-account steamcmd inside container → copy to `@ModName` folder + keys → `-mod=` via GAME_PARAMS recreate) | Steam Workshop 221100 | none (reuse existing DayZ owning account) | high mechanism / medium on exact log confirmation |
| conan | workshop-steamcmd-place (image's `GAME_MOD_IDS` downloads; Nxeon must add copy-to-Mods + modlist.txt write) | Steam Workshop 440900 | none | high on download / medium on activation step |

**Cross-cutting finding**: tested Steam's public `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails` API against 5 real workshop items across 4 different appids (730-collection, 4000, 221100 ×2, 440900) — every single one returned an empty `file_url`. Steam Workshop content is **never** directly HTTP-downloadable for any of these games; steamcmd (or the game's own Steam-integrated downloader) is mandatory in all cases. mod.io was checked and found not applicable to any of these 5 families (no evidence any of them publish through mod.io — they're all Steam-Workshop-first, or GitHub-first for cs16/CS2-plugins).

No family in this batch is GATED or NONE — all 5 have a real, evidenced mechanism using credentials/accounts Nxeon already holds. The two soft spots worth a real (non-production-host) test before shipping: (1) whether GMod's `host_workshop_collection` accepts a bare single-addon id or strictly requires a real collection wrapper, and (2) the exact Conan/DayZ post-download file-placement steps, which are COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE rather than confirmed by reading Funcom/Bohemia's own automation code.
